assessments.reasoning: The 7.54 overview establishes the terminology boundary for the glossary claim. ABAP CDS encompasses DDL and DCL, data definitions use DDL, and SAP distinguishes ABAP CDS from HANA CDS. The glossary entry supplies the exact definition attributed to it.

The PDF’s page 75 text describes writing CDS access controls whose conditions can use classical authorization objects. Page 108 describes declarative authorization for CDS entities and editing DCL sources. These passages clarify the access-control use. They supply no edition mapping to the 7.54 glossary.

SAP’s 7.54 glossary identifies the language, places it within ABAP CDS, and connects its source code to the definition of CDS objects for access control. All material parts of the scoped identity claim occur in the entry. The overview and development guide clarify neighboring concepts.

challenge.method: Check whether database choice or shared CDS terminology permits identifying DCL with HANA CDS, DDL, or ABAP CDS as a whole. Check whether classical authorization objects are identified as the DCL language or whether the guide establishes the release attribution. Check whether the entry defines only an abbreviation or also specifies the language’s domain, objects, and source form.
challenge.results: The overview distinguishes the platform variants and identifies two languages within ABAP CDS. Using a HANA database does not collapse those distinctions. Classical authorization objects can contribute data to a condition. DCL expresses the access control. The inspected page extracts give no basis for attributing the guide’s wording to the 7.54 glossary. The definition expressly connects all three to DCL. Its scope is CDS access control, which gives no basis for extending the identity to every CDS object or authorization mechanism.

limitations: The entity denotes ABAP CDS DCL in the documented SAP scope. ABAP CDS technology, CDS DDL, HANA CDS and classic authorization roles each have their own boundaries.
